av_event.line_text: Ryan: That's actually dead clever. That's a skill, that. Most people'd just see a pair of shoes. I wouldn't have a clue. Hannah, my wife, says I dress like a geography teacher, which is an insult I've never recovered from.
av_event.what: While Ryan is talking, Liam's eyes drop below the camera to his lap three or four times, and the bluish light on his face brightens briefly as if a phone screen has lit up. He looks back up at the screen each time after a second or two.

text:
B: Hiya! Sorry, give me a sec, the dog's just shifted onto my foot. Right. I'm Ryan, I'm in Long Eaton, I teach history. How you doing?
A: Alright. Liam. Normanton, near Wakefield.
B: Oh, Wakefield! I took a school trip to the Hepworth once, lovely building, kids moaned the whole way. Is that a Trinity scarf behind you?
A: Yeah.
B: Rugby league. I'll be honest, I know nothing about it, beyond the odd Challenge Cup final on the telly. Are they doing alright?
A: Not really. Rubbish at the weekend.
B: Ha, join the club. Derby County, me. Lost again Saturday. I think I support them out of guilt at this point, you know, my dad got me into it and now I can't get out.
A: Yeah. My grandad's like that with Trinity. Tells you about players from like the sixties, every Sunday, same stories.
B: Oh, I'd love that. That's basically primary sources, that, I'd be writing it all down. Sorry, history teacher. What do you do, Liam?
A: Warehouse. Picking, off the M62. Part-time, mostly lates.
B: Oh, right! My dad were a forklift driver at a warehouse off the M1. Twenty-odd years.
A: Yeah? I had my counterbalance ticket. Work paid for it. It's lapsed now though. Keep meaning to redo it 'cause it pays a bit more.
B: You should, honestly. Sorry, I sound like I'm talking to a Year 11. But you should.
A: Ha. Yeah. Prob will.
B: I'm a hypocrite anyway, I've got a qualification I've half finished for about two years. Are them boxes behind you trainers?
A: Yeah, I resell 'em. Vinted, eBay. You look for stuff that's listed wrong, or the photos are rubbish, or someone just wants it gone quick, and you get in first. Then you clean 'em up, take decent photos, stick 'em back on for proper money. Sold some Jordans last week for double what I paid. Do you know what I mean, it adds up.
B: That's actually dead clever. That's a skill, that. Most people'd just see a pair of shoes. I wouldn't have a clue. Hannah, my wife, says I dress like a geography teacher, which is an insult I've never recovered from.
A: Ha.
B: Is that a controller on the bed as well? What do you play?
A: EA FC mostly. Call of Duty. With a couple of mates on headsets.
B: No way, I play FC with my old uni mates! I'm awful, mind. I just sort of run at people and hope. We've got a group chat that's basically them laughing at my defending.
A: Yeah, most people just sprint. You've got to hold it up a bit.
B: Hold it up a bit. See, that's the advice I need. Do you do it for money, the trainers, like proper side income?
A: Trying to. If it made enough I'd drop some hours. Maybe get a flat. I'm at my mum's still, so.
B: Nothing wrong with that, mate. Me and Hannah only bought ours in 2019, I were renting a box room till I were about twenty-eight. My mum still pops round every Sunday anyway, so it's like I never left.
A: Yeah. Mine does a roast Sundays. That's the best bit.
B: Oh, a proper Sunday roast, can't beat it. Hannah's on lates this week so it's beans on toast for my tea every night, honestly, it's grim.
A: Beans on toast is about my limit, to be fair.
B: Ha! Well that's two of us then. Do you know when they pay out for this, by the way? I've never done one before.
A: No idea. I asked the other fella. He didn't know either. Hopefully before—
